tldr: AndroidArena is a new Android-based benchmark and environment for evaluating LLM agents on cross-APP collaboration and constraint-adherent tasks, revealing that even state-of-the-art LLM agents struggle significantly due to weaknesses in understanding, reasoning, exploration, and reflection.
contributions: Open-sourced AndroidArena, a scalable benchmark based on Android OS for evaluating cross-APP collaboration and constrained tasks, with a semi-automated task construction method that reduces manpower costs.

Demonstrated that SOTA LLM agents underperform in daily OS tasks with success rates below 60% in cross-APP scenarios, and proposed fine-grained metrics identifying four key capability areas for improvement.
Provided empirical analysis on reflection failures and achieved a 27% improvement in success rate by integrating historical visited information and balancing exploration-exploitation.
methods: The authors built AndroidArena on the Android OS using UIAutomator for direct UI component operations, supporting both screenshot and compressed XML textual observations. They designed a Mobile Task Generator (MTG) that extracts APP functionalities via search engines and vector databases, generates instructions using LLMs with an Evol-Instruct strategy, and employs human annotators for verification. Evaluation uses adaptive metrics including longest common subsequence (LCS)-based alignment, Task Reward (TR), Task Completion Ratio (TCR), Reversed Redundancy Ratio (RRR), and GPT-4 judged Success Rate (SR).
results: All SOTA LLM agents achieved less than 60% success rate in cross-APP scenarios. GPT-3.5 achieved a 6x higher success rate than LLaMA2-70B. LLaMA2 exhibited weaknesses across all four dimensions (understanding, reasoning, exploration, reflection), and even GPT-4 showed weak reflection and exploration abilities. Integrating historical visited information into prompts and balancing exploration and exploitation improved success rate by 27%. The XML compression method achieved an 86.6% compression ratio.
limitations: The compressed XML observation still exceeds 10,000 tokens on average across tested APPs, posing context length challenges. The evaluation is limited to 13 pre-installed Google suite APPs. Existing step-wise matching metrics are imprecise for non-unique action sequences. Reflection weakness is attributed to low-quality trajectories and sparse environmental feedback, which remain partially unresolved.
